defects: The zero-row divergence is NOT a defect in BLME's kernel -- it is score_X's own normalization, and BLME is the one that is right. Analytic anchor, m orthonormal rows plus (n-m) zero rows, where the definition-consistent Vendi Score is exp(H) of the mixture {1/n x m, (n-m)/n}: at n=40, m=39 the truth is 40.000000 (all 40 samples ARE mutually distinct) and BLME returns 40.000000 while score_X returns 36.476108 = n^(m/n); at m=35 truth 32.710617, BLME 32.710617, score_X 25.223334; at m=20 truth 8.944272, BLME 8.944272, score_X 6.324555. score_X is exactly n^(m/n) in every case, i.e. it silently DROPS the degenerate rows from the spectrum: sklearn.preprocessing.normalize leaves a zero row at zero, so K_ii = 0, trace(K) = m < n, and weight_K's K/n is a SUB-probability spectrum summing to m/n -- entropy_q then takes the entropy of a non-normalized vector. Def. 3.1 requires a unit diagonal, which BLME enforces. So the reported +9.7% (1 zero row in 40), +29.7% (5) and +41.4% (20) -- all of which I reproduced exactly -- are score_X being wrong, not BLME. The all-zero agreement at 1.0 is coincidence (an empty positive-eigenvalue mask sums to 0).
AND it never fires: I counted exactly-zero rows across every cached layer of two real models -- 0 / 154,740 for gpt2 and 0 / 158,232 for pythia-160m. The divergence is unreachable on hidden states.
